code_discovery.notes: The duplicate-definition problem is real: capability/tool/role/adapter definitions are spread across Merge80 capability and contribution registries, MCP catalogue/resolver/gate, Forge capability bindings, AI Core authorization profiles and Command Bus adapter registry. Treat Merge80's TypeScript capability/contribution registry as the primary convergence target, while preserving MCP tool metadata, Forge role bindings and Command Bus handler adapters as projections/bindings rather than independent authorities.

/MASTER Software/Masters/Platform/Titan AI Core/Titan AI Core Master v0.5.0.zip

code_discovery.notes: A canonical registry foundation already exists in Merge80. Governed handler-binding primitives also exist: Command Bus maps capability to one adapter and rejects duplicate adapter registration; MCP declares tool capability plus handler and enforces capability before handler resolution; AI Core authorizes capabilities; Forge maps roles to capabilities. Main implementation is to bind these into one registry-owned capability definition with governed execution bindings, not create another registry.

code_discovery.notes: Merge80 has many canonical JSON schemas and widespread TypeScript/Zod runtime validation patterns, while Forge and AI Core provide JSON/artifact/plan validators. No generic JSON-Schema-to-TypeScript type generator or canonical schema compiler was found in the scanned active sources. The existing Merge80 capability registry is itself @ts-nocheck. Implement one deterministic generation pipeline from canonical schemas, with generated TS types plus runtime validators, instead of continuing hand-written parallel schema/type definitions.
code_discovery.exhaustion_evidence: Searched Titan MCP v1.5.14, Titan Forge v0.9.0-alpha.9, Titan AI Core v0.5.0, Titan Command Bus v0.5.4 and current canonical Merge80 for TypeScript/codegen/JSON-schema compiler patterns. Found Zod/manual TS schemas and validation infrastructure, but no generic JSON Schema -> TypeScript generator.
